messages:
Miriam: quick check — ran the new 13B-int4 vs 13B-int8 slices overnight, wanted to share the economics + signal summary
Miriam: TL;DR: int4 wins cost by ~48% on token price, but we see a small degradation on long-form recall (~2.8% absolute) and a tail latency increase on 99.9th pct for prompt length >1024
Raj: can you paste the slice numbers? rough is fine
Miriam: sample sizes: 1.2k eval prompts from product-rep slice, 5k synthetic QA prompts, 10k random prefix traffic sample. Metrics: BLEU-ish recall proxies + rerank fallback success rate
Clare: what was the batching config? those tail numbers depend a lot on batch thresholds
Miriam: batching: continuous batching enabled, target_batch_ms=12, max_batch=16 on both. int4 runs on q4f16 quant profile. int8 runs on q8 profile. hardware: a100-40 across both
Oliver: repro command i used for perf runs:
```
./run_infer --model 13b --quant q4f16 --batch_target_ms 12 --max_batch 16 --seq_len 2048 --warmup 200
```
Oliver: perf summary (median / 99.9th) tokens/sec: int8 420 / 320, int4 410 / 260
Miriam: cost calculation: unit compute cost normalized to int8=1. int4 = 0.52 (kernel+memory savings). So per-token $ cost roughly int8 $0.0012 -> int4 $0.00062
Eva: what about output quality? product cares about hallucination and rerank fallback hits
Miriam: quality proxies: exact-match recall on QA: int8 78.2% -> int4 75.4% (delta -2.8). Rerank fallback trigger rate increased from 4.5% -> 7.1% (delta +2.6pp)
Raj: that's a noticeable bump in fallback — how does that translate to user-observed latency and cost (since fallback invokes larger model)?
Miriam: modeled: assume fallback to hosted-14b @ 4x token cost and average extra tokens = 60 per fallback. Net token-cost delta when switching all traffic to int4 vs int8: cost_savings_tokens = base_cost_savings - fallback_penalty
Miriam: quick calc from slices -> if baseline traffic = 1M tokens/day: int8 cost = $1200/day, int4 raw cost = $620/day. Additional fallback cost = (#fallbacks * 60 tokens * cost_14b). For our traffic, fallback increase adds ~ $90/day, so net int4 still saves ~$490/day (~41% saving)
Clare: that seems strong. But product cares about QA recall drop; can we route a small % to int8 and majority to int4 to get best of both?
Oliver: yes — hybrid rollout: 90% int4, 10% int8 reduces fallback delta and recovers ~75% of quality. Quick sim: with 90/10 split, expected recall ~ 76.9% and cost ~ $760/day -> still ~37% down vs int8 baseline
Eva: for GTN/PLG pitch we need an explicit recommendation: safe default for trial customers vs premium
Miriam: recommendation draft: default / free tier: int4 with hybrid fallback 90/10 for latency-sensitive apps; enterprise / high-SLAs: int8 pinned or 80/20 canary with stricter eval sets. Add a feature flag: route based on prompt length and density (long prompts -> prefer int8)
Raj: any ops concerns? tail latency on >1024 prompts increased for int4 — could be our kernel falling back to slower path
Oliver: confirmed: int4's 99.9th bump aligns with KV-cache eviction heuristics at >1k tokens under current runtime. Patch idea: increase per-stream KV prefetch and bump continuous batch timeout to 15ms for long sequences to reduce tail. Will test impact on cost/latency
Miriam: A/B plan for next week: 1) Canary 5% int4 on production with monitoring on fallback rate, product-quality proxy, and token-econ. 2) Run perf with batch_target_ms 15 for longform sample and compare tail 99.9%
Eva: can we get a one-slide summary for GTN: unit-econ, expected quality delta, recommended defaults, and rollout flags?
Miriam: will produce. rough bullets: - unit econ: int4 ~ -48% compute cost; net after fallback ~ -41% - quality: recall delta -2.8pt (recoverable with 10% int8 hybrid) - perf: median similar, 99.9th improved with runtime tweaks - recs: default int4+90/10 hybrid, long-prompts prefer int8, enterprise opt-in int8
Raj: nit: include sensitivity bounds: if fallback increase > +6pp then re-evaluate; also include latency SLO impacts
Miriam: noted. I'll attach the short CSV with the raw slice numbers after this thread
ops-bot: Canary deploy queued: canary-id=canary-20260325-047, 5% traffic -> 13b-q4f16; monitors: fallback-rate, recall-proxy, token-econ
Clare: thanks — ping when the canary is live and when we have 24h metrics
Miriam: will do. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
